definitions.explanation: Showing a lack of proper respect, especially toward persons of high status, sacred things, or social superiors. Carries a serious, formal tone.

examples.japanese: それは{不敬|ふけい}な{発言|はつげん}だ。
{神社|じんじゃ}で{不敬|ふけい}な{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いは{慎|つつし}むべきだ。
examples.english: One should refrain from irreverent behavior at a shrine.

examples.japanese: {戦前|せんぜん}の{日本|にほん}では、{天皇|てんのう}に{対|たい}する{不敬|ふけい}は{厳|きび}しく{罰|ばっ}せられた。
examples.english: In prewar Japan, disrespect toward the Emperor was severely punished.

notes:
A formal word indicating a failure to show proper respect toward authority, the sacred, or social superiors. Historically, {不敬|ふけい}{罪|ざい} (lèse-majesté) was a criminal offense in Japan before the postwar legal reforms. Today the word is used more broadly but retains a serious, weighty tone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不敬|ふけい}{罪|ざい} — lèse-majesté; crime of disrespecting the emperor
- {不敬|ふけい}な{態度|たいど} — disrespectful attitude
- {不敬|ふけい}な{発言|はつげん} — disrespectful remark
- {不敬|ふけい}に{当|あ}たる — to constitute disrespect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {失礼|しつれい} — rude, impolite; everyday word for being rude, much lighter than {不敬|ふけい}
- {無礼|ぶれい} — discourteous, rude; stronger than {失礼|しつれい} but not as heavy as {不敬|ふけい}
- {冒涜|ぼうとく} — blasphemy, profanation; specifically desecrating something sacred
